mechanism: Additive bleeding risk; GI mucosal injury
message: Warfarin with an NSAID markedly increases the risk of serious bleeding, particularly gastrointestinal.
recommendation: Avoid if possible; use paracetamol for analgesia. If unavoidable, add gastroprotection and monitor INR closely.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Warfarin with aspirin increases bleeding risk.
recommendation: Combine only with a clear indication (e.g. mechanical valve); monitor for bleeding.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Ciprofloxacin can raise INR and bleeding risk in patients on warfarin.
recommendation: Check INR within 3-5 days of starting; consider dose adjustment.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Levofloxacin can raise INR in patients on warfarin.
recommendation: Monitor INR closely.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Metronidazole strongly potentiates warfarin and can cause major bleeding.
recommendation: Avoid, or reduce warfarin dose and monitor INR within 3 days.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Fluconazole markedly increases warfarin effect.
recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose and monitor INR closely.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Co-trimoxazole increases warfarin effect and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid if possible; otherwise monitor INR closely.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Clarithromycin can raise INR in warfarin-treated patients.
recommendation: Monitor INR; consider an alternative antibiotic.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Amiodarone increases warfarin effect for weeks to months.
recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose by about a third to a half and monitor INR.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Rifampicin markedly reduces warfarin effect.
recommendation: Monitor INR frequently; the warfarin dose often needs to be increased.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Direct oral anticoagulants with an NSAID increase the risk of bleeding.
recommendation: Avoid if possible; use paracetamol.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Anticoagulant plus antiplatelet therapy increases major bleeding.
recommendation: Use only with a clear indication and review the duration.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors increase rivaroxaban levels and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid the combination.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors increase apixaban levels and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid the combination or reduce the apixaban dose per the label.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB raises the risk of hyperkalaemia, hypotension and renal failure without benefit.
recommendation: Avoid dual RAAS blockade.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: An ACE inhibitor with a potassium-sparing diuretic raises the risk of hyperkalaemia.
recommendation: Check potassium and renal function within a week, then regularly.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: An ARB with a potassium-sparing diuretic raises the risk of hyperkalaemia.
recommendation: Check potassium and renal function within a week, then regularly.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: An ACE inhibitor with potassium supplements raises the risk of hyperkalaemia.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: An ARB with potassium supplements raises the risk of hyperkalaemia.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: A potassium-sparing diuretic with potassium supplements can cause dangerous hyperkalaemia.
recommendation: Avoid unless potassium is closely monitored.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Nitrates with a PDE5 inhibitor can cause profound, life-threatening hypotension. The combination is contraindicated.
recommendation: Do not co-prescribe. Allow at least 24 h (sildenafil/vardenafil) or 48 h (tadalafil) after the PDE5 inhibitor before any nitrate.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: MAO inhibitors with SSRIs can cause fatal serotonin syndrome. The combination is contraindicated.
recommendation: Do not co-prescribe; observe a washout period (about 2 weeks, 5 weeks after fluoxetine).
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: MAO inhibitors with tramadol risk serotonin syndrome and seizures.
recommendation: Do not co-prescribe.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: MAO inhibitors with pethidine can cause severe, sometimes fatal, reactions.
recommendation: Do not co-prescribe.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Linezolid with an SSRI can cause serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Avoid if possible; if essential, monitor closely for serotonin toxicity.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: An SSRI with tramadol raises the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures.
recommendation: Prefer an alternative analgesic or monitor closely.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Benzodiazepines with opioids can cause profound sedation, respiratory depression and death.
recommendation: Avoid unless alternatives are inadequate; use the lowest doses and shortest duration; monitor sedation and breathing.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors markedly raise simvastatin levels and the risk of rhabdomyolysis. The combination is contraindicated.
recommendation: Withhold simvastatin during the interacting course or choose a non-CYP3A4 statin (e.g. rosuvastatin, pravastatin).
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors markedly raise lovastatin levels and the risk of rhabdomyolysis. The combination is contraindicated.
recommendation: Withhold lovastatin during the interacting course.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Gemfibrozil with simvastatin greatly increases the risk of rhabdomyolysis.
recommendation: Avoid; use fenofibrate if a fibrate is needed.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Clarithromycin raises atorvastatin levels and myopathy risk.
recommendation: Limit the atorvastatin dose or withhold it during the antibiotic course.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: NSAIDs can raise methotrexate levels and toxicity, especially with high-dose methotrexate.
recommendation: Avoid with high-dose methotrexate; monitor blood counts and renal function with low-dose.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Co-trimoxazole with methotrexate can cause severe bone-marrow suppression.
recommendation: Avoid the combination.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Trimethoprim with methotrexate can cause severe bone-marrow suppression.
recommendation: Avoid the combination.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Omeprazole reduces the antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel.
recommendation: Use pantoprazole instead, or stop the PPI if not needed.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Esomeprazole reduces the antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel.
recommendation: Use pantoprazole instead.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Amiodarone raises digoxin levels and the risk of toxicity.
recommendation: Reduce the digoxin dose by about half and monitor levels.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Verapamil raises digoxin levels and can cause bradycardia and AV block.
recommendation: Reduce the digoxin dose and monitor levels and heart rate.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Ciprofloxacin raises theophylline levels and can cause toxicity (arrhythmia, seizures).
recommendation: Reduce the theophylline dose or use another antibiotic; monitor levels.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Clarithromycin raises theophylline levels.
recommendation: Monitor theophylline levels.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: NSAIDs raise lithium levels and the risk of toxicity.
recommendation: Avoid or monitor lithium levels closely.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: ACE inhibitors raise lithium levels and the risk of toxicity.
recommendation: Monitor lithium levels and renal function.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Thiazide diuretics raise lithium levels by about 25-40%.
recommendation: Avoid, or reduce the lithium dose and monitor levels.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Clarithromycin raises carbamazepine levels and can cause toxicity.
recommendation: Avoid or monitor carbamazepine levels.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Fluconazole raises phenytoin levels and the risk of toxicity.
recommendation: Monitor phenytoin levels and adjust the dose.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Ciprofloxacin greatly increases tizanidine exposure (severe hypotension, sedation). The combination is contraindicated.
recommendation: Do not co-prescribe.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review

message: Allopurinol raises azathioprine toxicity (severe myelosuppression).
recommendation: Reduce the azathioprine dose to about a quarter and monitor blood counts.
source: General drug-interaction/prescribing references (product labels, standard formularies); pending clinical review
